questions.question: What is the genetic material of living organisms made of?
Which statement best describes the structure of a DNA molecule?
options: A single chain of proteins wrapped around lipid molecules
A long chemical molecule made of two chains of smaller units joined together
A triple-stranded carbohydrate chain with metallic bonds
A short, circular ring of amino acids with no links

questions.question: What term is used to describe the entire collection of DNA within a cell?
How are the two chains in a DNA molecule arranged?
options: They are spiralled around each other in a double helix with cross-links
They lie completely flat and parallel without any connections
They are folded into a spherical shape with a single hollow core
They form a single straight line with branches at each end

questions.question: Why can we sometimes see DNA during an extraction experiment without using a microscope?
options: Individual DNA molecules are naturally large enough to see with the naked eye
The extraction process turns the DNA into a bright blue glowing liquid
Clumps of DNA can be seen when a large amount of it is extracted together
The DNA reacts with water to form solid, colorful crystals

questions.question: What are the tightly-packed structures of wound-up DNA in a genome called?
Where are the 23 pairs of chromosomes stored in a human body cell?
What are the specific sections of DNA in chromosomes that store instructions for inherited features called?
What is the main function of non-coding DNA sections?
options: They store instructions that control when gene information is used
They directly build the cell membrane
They act as a backup copy of the cell's energy source
They prevent the DNA from dissolving in water

questions.question: In which part of plant, animal, and fungi cells is the genetic material stored?
Where do bacteria store their genetic material?
What biological term describes the process of organisms passing on features to their offspring?
Which of the following is true about how offspring compare to their parents and siblings?
options: Offspring are always completely identical to one of their parents
Offspring usually vary and are not identical to their parents or one another, except for identical twins
Offspring are always completely identical to all of their siblings
Offspring show no resemblance at all to their parents

questions.question: Which types of features can be inherited by offspring?
options: Only features caused by instructions in the genetic material
Only features acquired through heavy physical exercise
Any features caused by the surrounding environment
All features caused by diet and lifestyle choices

questions.question: Why can a person not pass a scar they received from an accident on to their children?
options: Scars are kept in the nucleus but are deleted during reproduction
Features caused by lifestyle and the environment cannot be inherited
Scars are dominant traits that skip a generation
The genetic material is temporarily damaged by scars
